correctness.rationale: The domain is all 32 binary centers of length five and 64 binary targets of length six. Each target has exactly its genuine distinct one-deletion predecessors; a covering must select one when that target remains uncovered. Branching over every predecessor is exhaustive. A candidate covers exactly seven targets, so an uncovered count larger than seven times the remaining capacity safely prunes the branch. Complete C++ and independently implemented Python searches rule out cardinalities at most eleven; both obtain exactly six canonical coverings at size twelve, verify every target of every covering and independently obtain three orbit pairs under complementation and reversal. No inference from a partial search or timeout is made.

value.rationale: Determines a natural exact single-insertion covering capacity at binary center length five and classifies all optimal constructions, identifying three genuinely different symmetry classes and exact labeled count six. The structural equality-case information is absent from the adjacent short-center Grozea table and is useful as a sharp benchmark for finite-alphabet insertion-covering constructions. This is not a routine restatement of large-alphabet bounds or a random isolated numerical computation; no asymptotic or general-length significance is claimed.
